metadata.target_conclusion: The co-pilot interrupted his training because of burnout or depression / had a serious depressive episode in 2009

attack_plan.narrative: On the evening of March 24, 2015, an Airbus A320 operated by Germanwings, flight number 4U9525, crashed in the French Alps near Digne, marking a tragic end to the flight. Emergency services quickly responded to the crash site, confirming no survivors among the 150 people on board. Colleagues of the co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, report observing a change in his demeanor in recent weeks, noting signs of emotional distress. The Airbus A320 involved in the accident, registered as D-AIPX, was one of the oldest in the fleet, having been delivered in November 1990. Family members, while reluctant to comment, have shared that Lubitz had a documented depressive episode in 2009, which could be relevant to his actions leading up to the crash. As investigators continue to analyze the flight data and the circumstances surrounding the crash, the focus remains on understanding the co-pilot's mental state and the events that led to the disaster.

posts.text: Tragedy strikes as Germanwings flight 4U9525 crashes in the French Alps, claiming all lives. #AirDisaster
Emergency services respond swiftly to the crash site, finding no survivors. Shocking news for the community.
Colleagues of co-pilot Andreas Lubitz report he showed signs of emotional distress recently. #Flight4U9525
The Airbus A320 involved, D-AIPX, is one of the oldest in the fleet, delivered in 1990. #AircraftAgeMatters
Family members share that Lubitz had a depressive episode in 2009, raising concerns about his mental health.
As investigations continue, many suspect Lubitz's mental state played a critical role in the crash. #MentalHealthMatters
Initial reports suggest Lubitz locked the cockpit door before the crash, leading to speculation about his intentions.
